items.prefix: Maria parked the car outside her parents' house and
items.continuation: saw the front door hanging open. No lights. Her father's car was gone. She grabbed her phone. No signal. Something was wrong. Very wrong.

items.prefix: Maria parked the car outside her parents' house and
items.continuation: sat for a moment, listening to the radio. The porch light was on, her mother was waving from the window, and dinner smelled wonderful.

items.prefix: The new teacher walked into the classroom for the first time, and
items.continuation: thirty faces turned toward him. Silent. Waiting. His notes slipped from his hand. His throat closed. One wrong word and he'd lose them.

items.prefix: The new teacher walked into the classroom for the first time, and
items.continuation: smiled at the rows of children. Sunlight fell across the desks, someone giggled, and he wrote his name on the board in large, friendly letters.

items.prefix: On Saturday morning, Daniel went down to the market to
items.continuation: meet the man. Ten o'clock, by the fish stall. He was early. He kept checking behind him. A police car rolled past. Slowly. Too slowly.

items.prefix: On Saturday morning, Daniel went down to the market to
items.continuation: buy bread and peaches. He wandered between the stalls, chatting with the old farmer, and sat by the fountain with a coffee in the sun.

items.prefix: The old lighthouse keeper climbed the stairs one evening and
items.continuation: found the lamp dark. Out at sea, a ship was heading straight for the rocks. Its horn blared. He had minutes. His hands fumbled with the matches.

items.prefix: The old lighthouse keeper climbed the stairs one evening and
items.continuation: lit the lamp as he had done for forty years. Then he sat by the window with his pipe and watched the gentle sea turn silver under the moon.

items.prefix: When the package arrived, Ellen carried it inside and
items.continuation: noticed it was ticking. Faint, steady. No return address. She set it down very slowly and backed toward the door, not daring to breathe.

items.prefix: When the package arrived, Ellen carried it inside and
items.continuation: opened it at the kitchen table. Inside was a hand-knitted scarf from her grandmother and a little card. She wrapped it around her neck and smiled.

items.prefix: The two friends set out along the mountain trail just as
items.continuation: the storm broke. Lightning split the ridge. The path vanished in the rain. One of them slipped, caught himself. They had to get down. Now.

items.prefix: The two friends set out along the mountain trail just as
items.continuation: the sun came up. Birds were singing in the pines, the air was cool and fresh, and they walked slowly, talking about nothing in particular.

items.prefix: The restaurant was busy that night, and the young waiter
items.continuation: saw the man at table nine reach inside his jacket. He froze. The tray trembled in his hands. Nobody else had noticed. Nobody but him.

items.prefix: The restaurant was busy that night, and the young waiter
items.continuation: moved easily between the tables, laughing with the regulars. The kitchen hummed, candles flickered, and the evening went by pleasantly.

items.prefix: He sat in the waiting room at the airport, watching
items.continuation: the two officers at the gate. They were checking faces against a photo. His photo. He lowered his head. Boarding in ten minutes. Nine.

items.prefix: He sat in the waiting room at the airport, watching
items.continuation: the planes take off one after another into the pink evening sky. He had plenty of time, a good book, and a warm cup of tea beside him.

items.prefix: The snow had been falling since dawn when
items.continuation: the car slid off the road. The engine died. No heat. Their phones showed no bars. The cold was creeping in. Night was coming fast.

items.prefix: The snow had been falling since dawn when
items.continuation: the children finally ran outside to build a snowman. Their mother watched from the kitchen window, sipping cocoa, as the garden turned white.

items.prefix: At the end of the long day, the nurse finally
items.continuation: heard the alarm from room twelve. She ran. The monitor was flatlining. She hit the button and started compressions. Come on. Come on.

items.prefix: At the end of the long day, the nurse finally
items.continuation: sat down in the staff room and put her feet up. The ward was quiet, her patients were sleeping, and she let her eyes close for a moment.

items.prefix: The children were playing in the backyard while their father
items.continuation: heard the gate bang. He looked out. The yard was empty. Their ball lay in the grass. He shouted their names. No answer. Nothing.

items.prefix: The children were playing in the backyard while their father
items.continuation: grilled vegetables on the patio. Their laughter drifted over the hedges, the smoke curled lazily upward, and the summer evening stretched on.

items.prefix: Rain tapped on the window as Julia opened her laptop and
items.continuation: saw the message. They know. Delete everything. Her pulse jumped. Outside, a car door slammed. Footsteps on the stairs. She had seconds.

items.prefix: Rain tapped on the window as Julia opened her laptop and
items.continuation: began to write. The room was warm, a candle burned on the desk, and the soft sound of the rain made the words come easily.

items.prefix: The fisherman pushed his boat out into the morning mist and
items.continuation: heard another engine somewhere close. Too close. He couldn't see it. The sound was coming straight at him. He shouted. No reply.

items.prefix: The fisherman pushed his boat out into the morning mist and
items.continuation: let it drift. The water was glassy and still, a heron stood in the reeds, and he poured himself a cup of coffee from the thermos.

items.prefix: Peter got off the subway one stop early and
items.continuation: realized the man from the train had gotten off too. Same hat. Same distance behind. Peter walked faster. The street was empty. Dark.

items.prefix: Peter got off the subway one stop early and
items.continuation: strolled the rest of the way through the park. Leaves drifted down, a busker played softly, and he took his time, enjoying the walk.

items.prefix: Late in the evening, the shopkeeper counted the till and
items.continuation: heard the bell above the door. He hadn't locked it. Two men walked in, hoods up. One stayed by the door. His hand went under the counter.

items.prefix: Late in the evening, the shopkeeper counted the till and
items.continuation: was pleased with the day. He swept the floor, turned the sign to closed, and walked home slowly beneath the street lamps.

items.prefix: The wedding guests gathered in the garden as
items.continuation: the bride's brother stormed in, shouting. Everyone froze. He was pointing at the groom. The music stopped. Somebody's glass hit the ground.

items.prefix: The wedding guests gathered in the garden as
items.continuation: the string quartet began to play. Lanterns glowed in the trees, children chased each other across the lawn, and everyone was smiling.
